signature: u32 Sound_SeqField_GetByteDefault3C(SoundSeqRecord* rec, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 index)

evidence: NEW: the sole caller is the now-confident Sound_SeqVoice_FillDescriptor; accessor type 0, the 0x3C default and the 0xFF mask are all visible in the body.

name: Sound_SeqField_GetFlag_Off04
signature: u32 Sound_SeqField_GetFlag_Off04(SoundSeqRecord* rec, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 index)
summary: Boolean field (accessor type 4 on rec+4): returns 1 when the field exists and its low byte is non-zero, else 0.
evidence: NEW: caller Sound_SeqVoice_FillDescriptor is now confident; the body's 'exists && (value & 0xFF) != 0' is a flag test, matching the name.

name: Sound_SeqField_GetByte_Off04
signature: u32 Sound_SeqField_GetByte_Off04(SoundSeqRecord* rec, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 index)

name: Sound_SeqField_GetByteDefault7F
signature: u32 Sound_SeqField_GetByteDefault7F(SoundSeqRecord* rec, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 index)

evidence: NEW: the sole caller Sound_SeqVoice_FillDescriptor is confident; accessor type 1 and the 0x7F default are visible. That 0x7F is a velocity/volume maximum is plausible but not proven.

name: maybe_Ui_Element_GetMetricA
summary: Calls virtual slot +0x14 of the element interface at self+0x24, converts the result with VectorSignedToFloat and returns it; the caller uses the value as a scale in a layout computation.
evidence: NEW: the caller (0x006EF8C4) is now named Math_Matrix44_Multiply, a name that cannot be right for a 44-byte UI accessor, so the caller side gives no support. The body is a pure virtual-getter wrapper; which metric (+0x14) is returned stays unknown.

name: maybe_Ui_Element_GetMetricB
summary: Same wrapper for virtual slot +0x10 of the element interface at self+0x24 (converted to float); the twin of 0x00663418, which uses slot +0x14.
evidence: NEW: the caller is now named Math_Vector_FloatToFixed, itself a doubtful name, so no support there. The pair's slot difference is visible but neither metric's meaning is.

name: MonsterBook_CompareSortIndex
signature: bool MonsterBook_CompareSortIndex(u32 arg1, u32 lhsId, u32 rhsId, u32 arg4)
summary: Ordering predicate for monster-id sorts: resolves both ids through the monster/data table (0x0063E3C8) and returns lhs->+0x11 < rhs->+0x11 (the record's sort index).
evidence: NEW: the caller is now the confident std_introsort_monsterId8, whose comparator must be this function, and the two lookups plus the byte compare at +0x11 are visible. The 'MonsterBook' label follows from the sorted id type.

name: maybe_Text_Window_IsPointInScrollArea
summary: Scroll-edge test: builds the cursor rectangle from the window's cursor position (+0x78) shifted by +/-2 and the area record at win+0x2D4 (+0x10..+0x16) plus the window extents (+0x2BC/+0x2C0), then asks 0x005CED04 whether the cursor is still inside.
evidence: NEW: the tail callee resolved to Field2D_Sprite_SetGlyphIcon, a name that cannot be right for a text window (the old evidence gives the same address as 0x005CED04), so the call chain is not fully trustworthy. The name therefore stays maybe_.

name: maybe_Text_SpanCursor_PickRandomOffset
signature: int maybe_Text_SpanCursor_PickRandomOffset(int spanOwner, int* cursor, int lineStart)
summary: Chooses an x offset for the text span cursor: Math_RandRangeInt picks a width in [w,w+1] and a sign, the largest of three candidates (random, current cursor offset, box edge) is taken, and a zero result is re-rolled once with the opposite sign.
evidence: NEW: all three callers are the maybe_Text_SpanCursor_* family (Init, PeekVisible, StepMultiline), so the span-cursor context is consistent; but those callers are themselves unconfirmed, so the name stays maybe_.

name: maybe_Text_Style_GetField15
summary: Returns the signed byte at +0x15 of the text style record reached through self+4 -> +0x298. It is a plain field accessor; what the field means is unknown.
evidence: NEW: the caller is now named Field2D_MapChip_TriggerWalkEvent, an implausible name for a text-style getter, and the sibling 0x00667068 is still maybe_Text_Style_GetField12. With the caller unreliable, the field's meaning remains open.

name: maybe_Text_Style_GetField12B
summary: Second read path for byte +0x12 of the text style record (self+4 -> +0x298), identical body to maybe_Text_Style_GetField12 (0x00667068); only the vtable entry differs.
evidence: NEW: the caller resolved to Field2D_MapChip_SetWalkTriggerState (again implausible) and the original twin is still unnamed. The body is the same one-byte read, so the name is kept as maybe_.

name: maybe_MoLive_Stream_ReadPcm
signature: int maybe_MoLive_Stream_ReadPcm(MoLiveStream* self, u32* out, u32 outWords)
summary: Reads decoded PCM out of the MoLive packet ring (f_30/f_34/f_3C) and circular sample buffer (f_54/f_58/f_5C/f_60), memmove-ing the wrapped range and growing the buffer via 0x00617298; returns the number of words written.
evidence: NEW: the caller is still MoLive_Decoder_GetPacket and the intact parts match the ring-buffer idiom, but the readable body contains halt_baddata, software_interrupt and func_0x... trampolines - per the project rule a damaged body keeps maybe_ and confidence <= 0.3.

name: maybe_Ui_Scene_EnsureCreated
summary: Lazily creates the shared 0x21C-byte UI scene object (vtable 0x007829E0, the same object type 0x00623914 creates) when the init byte is set, then returns the negation of Ui_LoadingScreen_IsFinished, i.e. 'the loading screen is still running'.
evidence: NEW: the callees are now named - Ui_LoadingScreen_IsFinished plus the allocator/vtable pair 0x0011FE8C/0x007829E0 used by 0x00623914. The old 'Svc_IsSubsystemReady' put this in the SDK services and called the value 'ready', while the body returns !isFinished of the loading screen.

name: maybe_Actor_ReleaseComponent
summary: Teardown of a component object: releases the sub-object at +4 (when present) and then recycles the enclosing object at self-0x220. Both callees currently carry unrelated merged names (Model_Equip_ApplyCommand, maybe_Ui_Label_SetFromCharPairB), so the real helpers are unidentifiable.
evidence: NEW: neither callee name is trustworthy (one is an equipment command, the other a label builder), so no new support arrived; only the +4 sub-object release and the -0x220 enclosing base are visible.

name: Actor_OnEvent
summary: Component event handler: events 0 and 6 drive the two 2D actor routines on the base object at -0x258, events 2/3 enable/disable the sub-object at -0x20C through its slot +0x14, and every event is then forwarded to the handler at f_18 via slot +0x84.
evidence: NEW: the event-0/6 callees are now named (Actor2D_UpdateFacingToTarget, Actor2D_ResetPartsIfIdle) and the eventId switch plus the final forward are visible; the -0x258 base is the actor object. The individual event meanings remain opaque, hence 0.5.

name: maybe_Actor_FindEffectComponentValue
summary: Asks the actor's component manager (vtable +0x2C) for the component of a given type, walks that component's linked list for the entry whose vtable is 0x007AE8A4 and returns its +0x78 value (effect frame/handle), or 0.
evidence: NEW: the caller is the confident Ui_PokerWindow_ResolveCardObjects and the effect accessor is maybe_Gfx_Effect_GetOwnerEffect, so 'find the effect component' holds. What +0x78 stores (frame vs handle) is not proven.

name: maybe_Field2D_Map_DetachOverlay
signature: void maybe_Field2D_Map_DetachOverlay(void* self, u32 arg2, u32 object, int apply)
summary: Releases the object at f_338 through its virtual destructor and always clears f_338; when `apply` is set it then runs Field2D_Actor_CheckCollisionBox on the passed object. It does not install a new overlay, contrary to the old summary.
evidence: NEW: the 0x005BDA18 callee is now the confident Field2D_Actor_CheckCollisionBox (0.60), whose own header lists 0x00670DB0 as a caller - not an 'install overlay' helper. So the function detaches/releases the slot and re-checks collision.

name: maybe_Field2D_Map_RebuildMoveController
summary: Rebuilds the object at f_A0: when f_58 still points at the inline default (+0x50) it releases the old object and creates a new one from self+0x70 with the descriptor {0x0070D454, 0x0067121C, self}; otherwise it calls the sprite-node reset path (0x005C72CC). The builder 0x005BE5A8 has no catalog entry.
evidence: NEW: the else-branch callee is now named Field2D_SpriteNode_ResetCallback, and the f_A0 slot is also written by the tween-move factory at 0x00671B14, so f_A0 is a movement/controller slot. The old 'PrimaryObject' name said nothing about that.

name: maybe_Field2D_Map_RebuildAppearanceNode

evidence: NEW: the builder callee is now the confident Field2D_SpriteNode_CreateAppearanceNode, so the function rebuilds an appearance node, not a generic 'overlay'. 0x00671A30 is a byte-identical twin of this one.

name: maybe_Field2D_Map_RebuildAppearanceNodeB

name: maybe_Field2D_Map_UpdateOverlaySprite
summary: Two-call vtable slot: Field2D_SpriteNode_Draw on the map object, then maybe_Field2D_Sprite_CheckViewBounds(map) - draw the 2D sprite and let the view-bounds/callback step run.
evidence: NEW: both callees now have names (Field2D_SpriteNode_Draw, 0.55; maybe_Field2D_Sprite_CheckViewBounds, 0.40) and they are draw/update operations, contradicting the old 'clear then reset' summary. 0x00671AFC is a byte-identical twin.

name: maybe_Field2D_Map_UpdateOverlaySpriteB

evidence: NEW: same two named callees as its twin; the old 'ResetOverlayB' wording is corrected for the same reason (draw/update, not clear/reset).

name: Field2D_Map_CreateTweenMove
signature: void Field2D_Map_CreateTweenMove(void* self, u32 arg2, u32 dir, u32 duration, u32 mode)
summary: Releases the controller at f_A0 and creates a new 2D tween-move controller for the map: Field2D_Sprite_CreateTweenMoveAlt(&self->f_70, self+8, three builder args, &{0x0070D718, 0x00671AFC, self}), then installs it in f_A0.
evidence: NEW: the builder callee is now the confident Field2D_Sprite_CreateTweenMoveAlt (0.60), whose header names 0x00671B14 as its caller and vtable 0x78368C as the installed controller - so the object created is a tween-move controller, not an 'overlay object'.

evidence: NEW: the callee is the confident Mem_BitmapPool_Init and the body is the same two-call shape as the startup registrar at 0x00678A88. The old 'Field_InitPackedTableReader' name had no support: no table reader is called.

name: maybe_Gfx_RenderCallback_Dispatch

name: Gfx_GpuCmd_WriteRect
summary: Builds a rectangle command block: converts rect[0..3] to float / 3-bit fixed point, copies rect[4]/rect[5], sets the descriptor flag byte to 1, appends it to the writer's command chain through 0x00658240/0x00657824 and returns the writer.
evidence: NEW: all eight callers are now named draw passes (Gfx_ModelInstance_DrawFullscreenQuadPass, DrawRectPass, DrawTexCoordPass, ...), which all need a screen-space rectangle; the fixed-point conversion and the append chain are visible in the body.

name: Container_NameHashFindEmbedded
signature: void Container_NameHashFindEmbedded(HashIterPair* out, NameHashMap* map, const NameHashKey* key)
summary: Name-map lookup for maps whose node embeds its key/value at node+0x10: descends the rb-tree by hash (key[0]), then compares the 0x40-byte stored name with key[1] and returns the (node, insertion hint) pair.
evidence: NEW: the caller is now the confident Fs_NamedObject_GetOrCreate, exactly a name-keyed registry with insert-on-miss, and the body matches the non-embedded twin 0x006F322C with every read routed through node+0x10.

name: maybe_Text_NormalizeKanaName
summary: Name normaliser for name entry: the readable body is truncated to a single call of the wide strlen 0x00100B74 on the kana table at 0x007C2204 (Ghidra marks it 'does not return'), so only the table contents (U+30F4/U+309B/U+3046/'%') and the caller identify it.
evidence: NEW: the caller is now named Actor_CompareNames, which fits 'normalise a name so that names compare equal', but the body is truncated after one call, so the rewrite itself is not verifiable here. Kept at 0.35.

name: maybe_std_RbTree_EraseRebalanceEntry1
summary: 4-byte Thumb entry (0x0070D126) into the shared red-black erase/rebalance body at 0x0070D12E: it only establishes the register frame before falling through; nothing references it.
evidence: The three decompilations are identical apart from the missing prologue registers (unaff_r6/unaff_r7), so per the project's damaged-decompilation rule this stays maybe_ at 0.3. functions_index.json still records it as a 4-byte thumb entry right after 0x0070D0F8.

name: maybe_std_RbTree_EraseRebalanceEntry2
summary: Second 4-byte Thumb entry (0x0070D12A) into the same red-black erase/rebalance body; no distinct behaviour of its own.
evidence: Same situation as 0x0070D126: identical body modulo the unaff_r* frame registers, no branch target in asm/text/*.s, so the rule for damaged decompilation keeps it maybe_ at 0.3.

name: maybe_std_RbTree_EraseRebalance
signature: void maybe_std_RbTree_EraseRebalance(RbTree* tree, RbNode* header, RbNode** iter, u8 colour)
summary: Canonical red-black delete fix-up (the four symmetric sibling cases with colour flips/rotations) that then pushes the removed node onto the tree's free list and decrements the entry count; it is the real body behind the 0x0070D126/0x0070D12A entries.
evidence: NEW: std_RbTree_ListNodeUnlink is now a confident callee (the free-list push at the end), but the body still reads unaff_r6/unaff_r7 for the tree/colour registers, so the damaged-decompilation rule keeps confidence at 0.3.

name: maybe_Container_HashMap_FindByNameB
summary: Type-checked registry lookup over the global hash table g_00713AE0/AE4/AE8: finds an entry whose vtable type id is 0x007E2018 and whose 0x40-byte key (words +0x14..+0x50) matches the request; returns the entry or 0.
evidence: NEW: the caller is now the confident Model_LoadHitEffectResources and the A twin 0x007135D4 is still maybe_Container_HashMap_FindByNameA, so the B suffix and the 'by name' key remain unconfirmed; the 0x40-byte comparison through 0x00123660 is visible.

name: maybe_std_push_heap_itemName8_entry
signature: void maybe_std_push_heap_itemName8_entry(u32* base, u32 hole, u32 top, u32 value)
summary: Sift-up (__push_heap) for 8-byte records: compares with std_less_itemId8 and moves records with 0x0011FFFC while walking (hole-1)/2 toward the top; base/hole/top/value arrive in registers Ghidra could not track.
evidence: NEW: the comparison callee is now the confident std_less_itemId8, so the heap algorithm is clear - but the record is compared by item id while the name claims 'itemName8', and all four parameters are unaff_r*. The record type and the name/id distinction stay unproven, so a maybe_ prefix is restored.

name: Text_SortPairsByFloatKey
signature: void Text_SortPairsByFloatKey(u32* first, u32* last, int depth)
summary: Introsort over 8-byte pairs whose comparison is the float in the second word ((float)a[1]): median-of-three quicksort within a 0x80-byte threshold, heap-sort fallback and insertion pass, used by Text_LayoutColumns.
evidence: NEW: the caller is the confident Text_LayoutColumns and the comparator is visibly the float at +4 of each pair. The old name asserted that float is a Y coordinate; nothing in the body says Y, so the name is corrected to the proven property.

name: std_introsort_itemEntry
signature: void std_introsort_itemEntry(u32* first, u32* last, int depth, u32 context)
summary: Introsort for 4-byte item rows {u16 id; u8; u8}: median-of-three pivot via maybe_Item_SortByEntryKey16, depth-limited recursion with a push-heap fallback and the 0x41-byte threshold; used by the two maybe_Ui_DataPanel row sorts.
evidence: NEW: the callers are the two maybe_Ui_DataPanel sort routines (whose tables are 4-byte rows) and the depth-0 path calls the confident std_push_heap_itemId8_entry. The body copies a u16 plus a u8 and steps its u32* by one, i.e. stride 4, so the old 'itemEntry8' suffix misstated the record size and is dropped rather than replaced by another guess.

name: maybe_Actor_Node_InitState
signature: void maybe_Actor_Node_InitState(ActorComponent* self, u32 p1, u32 p2, int p3)
summary: Vtable method (vtable 0x007290C0): reads the actor state byte f_48C and, when it is neither 2 nor 4, points the node base at self+0x488; the remainder is lost to halt_baddata.
evidence: NEW: there is still no named caller or callee; the body contains halt_baddata, unaff_r5 and a call to a 0x01D005CC trampoline, so the damaged-decompilation rule keeps the name maybe_ at 0.3.

name: maybe_Actor_Node_CheckBounds
summary: Vtable method (vtable 0x00729028): the readable body is almost entirely lost - only coordinate arithmetic on the self pointer and in_ZR/in_CY/unaff_r8 conditionals survive before halt_baddata, so 'CheckBounds' is only the previous hypothesis.
evidence: NEW: no caller or callee is available and the body is a damaged decompilation (in_ZR/in_CY flag registers, impossible pointer arithmetic), so the name and the 0.3 confidence stay.
